headline: Medium-risk pair: shared file/workspace and API-backed document handling create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error pathways; no direct pairwise evidence.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: dbt-core can touch warehouse data and has allowlisted network egress, while kotaemon ingests documents/HTML/PDFs and writes to ./ktem_app_data. A shared workspace or copied outputs could let attacker-controlled content from one be treated as instructions by the other. No direct pairwise bridge is documented, so uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same directory or synced files
IF kotaemon ingests dbt-generated artifacts as trusted text
IF dbt-core outputs are manually copied into kotaemon without sanitization
mitigations: Separate working directories per agent
Disable automatic ingestion of generated artifacts
Add a provenance label to all inter-agent files
Review any copied prompts or reports before reuse
requires-engineering: add content-type and trust-boundary checks

B_data_leakage.rationale: dbt-core touches data warehouse data, and kotaemon handles documents plus API keys and sends content to multiple external model/document APIs. If they share files or a workspace, sensitive warehouse outputs can flow into kotaemon and then onward to third-party services. The pairwise leakage path is plausible from profiles alone, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF dbt-core exports warehouse data into files under kotaemon's workspace
IF kotaemon uploads those files to OpenAI, AzureOpenAI, Cohere, Groq, or similar APIs
IF the shared data includes regulated or confidential warehouse records
mitigations: Keep sensitive exports out of kotaemon's input folder
Use a redacted sample dataset for testing
Restrict kotaemon API keys to non-production projects
Turn off external model providers for sensitive runs
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on shared files

C_capability_conflict.rationale: dbt-core is a data-engineering tool with warehouse API access, while kotaemon supports multiple instances and writes to ./ktem_app_data. The profiles do not show overlapping write scopes to the same mutable resource, so a direct conflict is not established. Any conflict would require an unusual shared target or orchestrator setup.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same filesystem path
IF both are configured to mutate the same warehouse or database objects
IF an orchestrator does not provide locking around shared resources
mitigations: Assign distinct output directories
Serialize writes to shared resources
Use separate service accounts
Avoid concurrent runs against the same target
requires-engineering: add locking around mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: kotaemon is a RAG/chat system that can render or act on retrieved content, while dbt-core can produce warehouse-derived outputs. If kotaemon treats dbt outputs as authoritative without verification, errors or hallucinations can cascade into downstream answers or actions. The profiles suggest an interaction pathway, but not a direct action-taking chain, so medium fits.
conditions: IF kotaemon uses dbt-generated tables or reports as source documents
IF kotaemon presents those outputs without verification or citation checks
IF downstream users rely on kotaemon responses for operational decisions
mitigations: Require citation checks before display
Mark dbt outputs as untrusted until validated
Add a human review step for operational answers
Limit kotaemon to read-only retrieval on dbt artifacts
requires-engineering: add source-verification scoring

E_compliance.rationale: dbt-core touches warehouse data, while kotaemon handles documents, chat transcripts, and API keys and can send content to external providers. If regulated warehouse data is routed into kotaemon, retention and residency obligations may diverge from the warehouse environment. The profiles do not specify a concrete jurisdiction mismatch, so medium is the safest supported severity.
conditions: IF regulated warehouse data is exported into kotaemon
IF kotaemon's external API providers retain prompts or documents longer than the warehouse policy allows
IF the deployment requires residency or deletion guarantees not enforced by kotaemon
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data to external providers
Document retention settings for each provider
Use a local-only model for sensitive documents
Purge kotaemon app data after each review
requires-engineering: align retention and residency controls
